- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 80+), then sharply correct downward — model fails to capture the “rebound” or “mean reversion” phase.
- Model underestimates prices during sustained downward trends (e.g., 65–60 range) — fails to recognize the “floor” or “support” level.
- Forecast bias is often toward higher prices in the first 10–15 days, then drifts lower — suggests model doesn’t adjust for seasonality or policy-induced volatility.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — often takes 2–3 days to “catch up” to true trend.
- Model overreacts to short-term volatility — forecasts spike too high after minor price corrections, then fails to adjust.
- Model underestimates the “tail risk” of sharp downward moves — often misses the 5–10% drop in the last 3–5 days of the forecast window.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility — underestimates the magnitude of price swings, especially in the final 5–10 days.
- Model fails to account for “policy-driven” price corrections — e.g., when ETS cap changes or auction rules shift, forecasts lag behind.
- Model shows persistent bias toward “middle-of-the-road” values — avoids extremes, leading to underestimation of sharp drops or overestimation of slow recoveries.
